strengths: Novel framework bridging classical phylogenetics and deep learning through conditionally site-independent rate matrices, addressing genuine limitation of i.i.d. sequence assumptions
Rigorous theoretical contributions with proven first-order approximation error bounds (Proposition 4.1) and exact Gillespie sampling conditions (Lemma 4.2)

Comprehensive experimental validation including synthetic codon validation (Section B.1), zero-shot VEP outperforming DASM/ProGen2/ESM-2 on 6/7 datasets, and epistatic interaction analysis via categorical Jacobian
Methodologically sound SHM correction (Eq. 5) using principled log-likelihood ratio without ad-hoc clamping, and Taylor-approximated guidance achieving 500-900× speedup

Excellent reproducibility with detailed protocols, 2M training transitions from 5 public sources, and extensive ablations in appendix (SNR weighting, single vs. paired conditioning, exact vs. approximate guidance)

Modest empirical improvements in several scenarios: COSINE (0.613) vs. DASM (0.596) on Koenig(H) is marginal, and only 0.005 gain vs. ProGen2 on Koenig(L); unclear when complex model is warranted over simpler DASM

Acknowledged but unresolved antigen-specificity gap: model scores don't align with binding affinity for arbitrary antigens (Section 4.2); guidance solution requires oracle fine-tuning; no experimental validation of designed sequences

strengths: Clear motivation addressing the gap between language models and evolutionary biology; well-articulated problem formulation
Rigorous theoretical framework with Proposition 4.1 (first-order approximation with O(t²) error) and Lemma 4.2 (Gillespie exactness) proven via uniformization
Large-scale experiments on ~2M transitions with comprehensive benchmarking including synthetic validation, DMS assays, guided sampling, and CDR optimization
Novel conditionally site-independent CTMC architecture elegantly balances expressivity and computational tractability
Clever technical contributions including TAG guidance with 500-900× speedup and principled selection score disentanglement
Extensive supplementary results with detailed ablations (SNR weighting, sampling error analysis, VEP variants) supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical theory-practice gap: Propositions 4.1-4.2 assume (Qθ(x)ℓ)_{xℓ,yℓ}=Q_{x,y}, but COSINE is trained on the approximate factorized likelihood (Eq. 2) that violates this. Authors acknowledge rates incur 'bias due to marginalization of unobserved intermediate states' on long branches, but Section C.1 shows SNR weighting didn't improve results. Theory provides intuition rather than guarantees.

Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements: VEP results show marginal gains over DASM (Koenig H 0.613 vs 0.596, Δ=0.017) and losses on some datasets (Koenig L Expression 0.508 vs ProGen2-Small 0.513). Only Adams dataset shows substantial gains; unclear if systematic improvement or outlier.

Unjustified experimental design choices: Fixed t=0.2 across all DMS assays without sensitivity analysis or justification; arbitrary Shanehsazzadeh dataset splitting by chain length (119 vs 120); only 4 DMS benchmarks selected despite many available in ProteinGym.

Guided Gillespie approximations (first-order Taylor + locally constant variance) defined in limit t→0 but applied at t=0.2. Section C.7 claims statistical equivalence between TAG and exact guidance but with only 15 samples—severely underpowered (p>0.05 tests lack power).

Conditional independence assumption still limits expressivity: Equation 2 cannot capture higher-order epistatic patterns. Figure S3 shows substantial KL divergence at ε=1.0 (maximal epistasis); claim of capturing epistasis is overstated.

Limited biological validation: Figure 3 categorical Jacobian shows expected CDR dependencies but lacks quantitative comparison to alternatives (e.g., does ESM2 capture these?). No validation that inferred selection scores match measured binding affinities beyond DMS correlation.
Narrow scope with unvalidated generalization: Tested only on antibodies where indels are rare; sequential mutation assumption is antibody-specific. Claims about broader applicability lack evidence.

Missing critical ablations: Contribution of pretrained ESM2 backbone unknown; whether improvements stem from COSINE innovations or large-scale pretraining unclear. No ablations on architectural choices.

Statistical rigor concerns: Most results lack error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Guided affinity maturation based on ~5 seeds × 3 repetitions=15 samples per condition. Comparison with DASM via per-site likelihood (62.3%) is marginal without distribution analysis.

Presentation issues: Memorization of germline residues motivation (page 1) never empirically addressed. Key limitations relegated to Section 6/appendices rather than upfront discussion. Paper is dense; core innovation obscured.

strengths: Strong theoretical contribution with rigorous mathematical framework: Proposition 4.1 establishing first-order approximation with O(t²) error bounds and Lemma 4.2 proving Gillespie sampling exactness using principled uniformization arguments

Novel and elegant approach bridging classical phylogenetic modeling with modern deep learning: conditioning site-specific rate matrices on full sequence context enables epistasis capture while maintaining tractability

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple scales: synthetic codon experiments validate theory in tractable setting; large-scale real data with ~2M transitions from ~120k clonal families; consistent outperformance on variant effect prediction (6/7 datasets in Table 1) and affinity optimization tasks

Methodologically sophisticated with well-designed innovations: SNR-weighted loss addresses branch-length bias; Taylor-approximated guidance (TAG) achieves 500-900× speedup; principled selection score derivation avoids DASM's ad-hoc constraints
Interpretable epistasis modeling: Categorical Jacobian (Figure 3) reveals biologically plausible inter-chain and intra-CDR dependencies; demonstrates model learns meaningful evolutionary dynamics
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: clear narrative, detailed appendices with training procedures and synthetic protocols, honest limitations discussion, pseudocode for algorithms

Limited scope and generalizability: only validated on antibodies, not general proteins; ignores insertions/deletions even though they're rare in antibodies; unclear if insights extend beyond immunology or if method generalizes to other protein evolution scenarios

Modest empirical improvements in several cases: VEP gains often incremental (Koenig (H) expression: 0.613 vs DASM 0.596 vs ProGen2 0.592); lacks statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; improvements don't clearly justify added model complexity over simpler baselines

Unexplained inconsistencies in inter-chain modeling: Table S2 shows single-chain sometimes outperforms paired conditioning, contradicting the inter-chain epistasis narrative; authors hypothesize training data composition but don't investigate; binding shows 0.12-point gains from pairing while expression shows only 0.006

Fixed branch length t=0.2 in VEP experiments not justified: selection score derivation uses small-t approximation but t=0.2 is not small; sensitivity analysis missing despite Section C.7 suggesting results vary with t; validity of approximation at t=0.2 unexplored

Categorical Jacobian analysis limited to single antibody: only one example (47D11) shown; consistency of epistatic patterns across different antibodies unstudied; unclear if patterns are CDR-specific or general

Consistent improvements over baselines on zero-shot variant effect prediction, particularly on non-human antibodies (Adams: 0.464 vs 0.231)
